result.title: On the Geometry of Multimodal Saturation: Riemannian VICReg
result.comment: 17 pages, 6 figures. Accepted to the Proceedings Track of the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations (NeurReps)
result.summary: In self-supervised learning, a third modality should improve, or at least preserve, performance. Across nine image-text-tabular datasets, we show that it instead harms performance: the trimodal model underperforms its own best bimodal subset in 55.6% of paired runs under VICReg. The same failure occurs in 51.1% of paired runs under SimSiam. We call this failure multimodal saturation. We propose that the failure lies in the alignment geometry. Riemannian VICReg (R-VICReg) generalizes classical VICReg: it aligns views by squared geodesic distance on learnable negative-curvature product factors and recovers VICReg exactly as curvature vanishes. Over the same 45 paired runs, R-VICReg raises the probability that the third modality helps from 44.4% to 64.4%, with gains concentrated where VICReg saturates.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在九个图像-文本-表格数据集上发现第三模态常导致性能下降（「多模态饱和」），并归因于对齐几何，提出在负曲率乘积流形上用测地距离对齐的 Riemannian VICReg，使第三模态有益的配对比例从 44.4% 提升到 64.4%。
AI.relevance_reason: 不直接涉及 VLM 推理，但其关于多模态对齐几何与模态增益被抑制的诊断，或可供核查 latent 表示中视觉信息是否被压制、贡献分配失当等问题；几何式对齐目标也可能为 latent 状态约束提供线索。
